issues.title: Are the SD-CWT Key Binding Token / SD-JWT key binding really necessary for use in MLS?
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body:
The Key Binding Token in SD-CWT provides the following functions:

- prove possession of the holder private key
- sign the specific set of disclosures used
- to prevent replay of the SD-CWT when a cnonce is present
- explicitly set the audience (ex: the room) if none is set 
- potentially have a smaller validity period than the CWT it contains
- include other holder-asserted claims

MLS provides a signature over the LeafNodeTBS struct and includes a signature key that needs to match the holder key in the SD-CWT. Replaying just an SD-CWT would be impossible without signing the LeafNode. It would also implicitly bind the audience to the the current MLS group (although not to an application-level structure like a MIMI room). In this way, we might be able to get away without having a KBT.

Likewise an SD-JWT can contain an optional key binding token. The signature over the LeafNodeTBS struct covers the signature key and that needs to match the holder key in the SD-JWT.

issues.title: Mention that an SD-JWT can contain a regular JWT
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body:
From [Section 4.1](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-selective-disclosure-jwt-22.html#name-issuer-signed-jwt)

"An SD-JWT has a JWT component that MUST be signed using the Issuer's private key. It MUST NOT use the none algorithm."

In other words, most JWTs can be conveyed as an SD-JWT with no changes.
